text:
alex: Heads up — saw a cluster of user sessions that never recovered after a short proxy idle (10s) -> clients stay in 'connecting' for minutes :confused:
mei: same, noticed spike in reconnect attempts and then 429s from global-rate-limiter right after the idle timeout fired
santiago: logs from edge-proxy: `session_close idle_timeout=10; suppress_new=true || rate_limit:exceeded` — looks like suppress_new is flipping on the same path the rate limiter uses for dedupe
jamie: is suppress_new our code that prevents immediate session re-creation to avoid billing dupes? we added it last quarter for cost reasons
alex: yes, it gates new session creation for N seconds after a close to avoid double-charging. But it appears to persist longer when the rate-limiter returns 429 concurrently
mei: repro steps I used:
```
# repro: open websocket -> wait 12s -> close socket from proxy side -> client reconnect flood
for i in {1..50}; do curl -H "Connection: Upgrade" ws://edge.local/connect; done
```
results: ~30% of clients see 429s, others get stuck connecting.
santiago: stack trace snippet from proxy on a stuck path:
```
2026-03-21T15:02:01Z proxy.INFO session_close id=abc idle=10
2026-03-21T15:02:01Z proxy.DEBUG apply_suppression session_id=abc window=30
2026-03-21T15:02:01Z limiter.WARN check_rate client=xx status=429
2026-03-21T15:02:01Z proxy.INFO session_reject reason=suppression_active
```
jamie: console UX shows the connection as "reconnecting" indefinitely; we don't surface suppression as a reason so support teams see a phantom problem
mei: also, dashboard metrics count these as reconnect attempts (spike), but billing subsystem only counts some of them. leads to SLO/ticket noise
santiago: hypothesis: the suppression flag is stored in an opaque in-memory ttl keyed by session token. rate-limiter paths run before the suppression TTL refresh, causing a race where a 429 prevents the code path that would have cleared suppression => suppression extends
alex: proposal A: make suppression keyed by client fingerprint + atomic compare-and-set to ensure 429 paths still clear suppression at end of flow
jamie: proposal B: add a short console-level mapping so operators see "suppression_active" as a reason (non-sensitive) and a dashboard chart for suppression-window count so we can correlate with rate-limiter spikes
mei: quick mitigation: reduce idle-suppression window from 30s -> 3s behind a feature flag for edge canary (will reduce double-charge risk slightly but fixes UX)
santiago: caution: reducing window increases risk of duplicate billing if a proxy double-closes. we need telemetry to measure double-charge before flip.
alex: can we create an eval: count(session_close->session_open within 2s that both reach billing service) across last 24h? if < 0.01% then we can try 3s canary
jamie: I'll add a console chart and a per-route suppression gauge in the next deploy. tagging: @eng-sre for alert tweaks
mei: I've added a feature-flag entry: `suppress_session_window_ms` default 30000, canary 3000 on edge-canary group. deploy-bot: rolling canary start for edge-canary flag set by jamie (id: FF-221)
deploy-bot: canary rollout: 5% -> 25% over 10m -> monitor metrics (suppressions, 429s, duplicate_billing_rate)
santiago: action items:
- jamie: console chart + human-readable reason mapping (P0)
- mei: telemetry query for duplicate billing (P1)
- alex: spike a fix for suppression race (CAS) (P0)
- eng-sre: watch canary and mute noisy reconnect alerts for 15m during test
jamie: ok I'll pick up the console work today. anyone want to pair on the CAS change?
alex: i'll pair after lunch.
mei: i'll run the duplicate billing query and report back here in ~1h. :thumbsup:
